content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: 77:1 Atténdite, pópule meus, legem meam: * inclináte aurem vestram in verba oris mei.
content.english: 77:1 Attend, O my people, to my law: * incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

segments.t: Atténdite, pópule meus, legem meam: * inclináte aurem vestram in verba oris mei.

content.latin: 77:2 Apériam in parábolis os meum: * loquar propositiónes ab inítio.
content.english: 77:2 I will open my mouth in parables: * I will utter propositions from the beginning.

segments.t: Apériam in parábolis os meum: * loquar propositiónes ab inítio.

content.latin: 77:3 Quanta audívimus et cognóvimus ea: * et patres nostri narravérunt nobis.
content.english: 77:3 How great things have we heard and known, * and our fathers have told us.

segments.t: Quanta audívimus et cognóvimus ea: * et patres nostri narravérunt nobis.

content.latin: 77:4 Non sunt occultáta a fíliis eórum: * in generatióne áltera.
content.english: 77:4 They have not been hidden from their children, * in another generation.

segments.t: Non sunt occultáta a fíliis eórum: * in generatióne áltera.

content.latin: 77:4 Narrántes laudes Dómini, et virtútes eius: * et mirabília eius, quæ fecit.
content.english: 77:4 Declaring the praises of the Lord, and his powers, * and his wonders which he hath done.

segments.t: Narrántes laudes Dómini, et virtútes eius: * et mirabília eius, quæ fecit.

content.latin: 77:5 Et suscitávit testimónium in Iacob: * et legem pósuit in Israël.
content.english: 77:5 And he set up a testimony in Jacob: * and made a law in Israel.

segments.t: Et suscitávit testimónium in Iacob: * et legem pósuit in Israël.

content.latin: 77:5 Quanta mandávit pátribus nostris nota fácere ea fíliis suis: * ut cognóscat generátio áltera.
content.english: 77:5 How great things he commanded our fathers, that they should make the same known to their children: * that another generation might know them.

segments.t: Quanta mandávit pátribus nostris nota fácere ea fíliis suis: * ut cognóscat generátio áltera.

content.latin: 77:6 Fílii qui nascéntur, et exsúrgent, * et narrábunt fíliis suis.
content.english: 77:6 The children that should be born and should rise up, * and declare them to their children.

segments.t: Fílii qui nascéntur, et exsúrgent, * et narrábunt fíliis suis.

content.latin: 77:7 Ut ponant in Deo spem suam, et non obliviscántur óperum Dei: * et mandáta eius exquírant.
content.english: 77:7 That they may put their hope in God and may not forget the works of God: * and may seek his commandments.

segments.t: Ut ponant in Deo spem suam, et non obliviscántur óperum Dei: * et mandáta eius exquírant.

content.latin: 77:8 Ne fiant sicut patres eórum: * generátio prava et exásperans.
content.english: 77:8 That they may not become like their fathers, * a perverse and exasperating generation.

segments.t: Ne fiant sicut patres eórum: * generátio prava et exásperans.

content.latin: 77:8 Generátio, quæ non diréxit cor suum: * et non est créditus cum Deo spíritus eius.
content.english: 77:8 A generation that set not their heart aright: * and whose spirit was not faithful to God.

segments.t: Generátio, quæ non diréxit cor suum: * et non est créditus cum Deo spíritus eius.

Psalmus 77(9-16)

content.latin: 77:9 Fílii Ephrem intendéntes et mitténtes arcum: * convérsi sunt in die belli.
content.english: 77:9 The sons of Ephraim who bend and shoot with the bow: * they have turned back in the day of battle.

segments.t: Fílii Ephrem intendéntes et mitténtes arcum: * convérsi sunt in die belli.

content.latin: 77:10 Non custodiérunt testaméntum Dei: * et in lege eius noluérunt ambuláre.
content.english: 77:10 They kept not the covenant of God: * and in his law they would not walk.

segments.t: Non custodiérunt testaméntum Dei: * et in lege eius noluérunt ambuláre.

content.latin: 77:11 Et oblíti sunt benefactórum eius: * et mirabílium eius quæ osténdit eis.
content.english: 77:11 And they forgot his benefits, * and his wonders that he had shewn them.

segments.t: Et oblíti sunt benefactórum eius: * et mirabílium eius quæ osténdit eis.

content.latin: 77:12 Coram pátribus eórum fecit mirabília in terra Ægýpti: * in campo Táneos.
content.english: 77:12 Wonderful things did he do in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, * in the field of Tanis.

segments.t: Coram pátribus eórum fecit mirabília in terra Ægýpti: * in campo Táneos.

content.latin: 77:13 Interrúpit mare, et perdúxit eos: * et státuit aquas quasi in utre.
content.english: 77:13 He divided the sea and brought them through: * and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel.

segments.t: Interrúpit mare, et perdúxit eos: * et státuit aquas quasi in utre.

content.latin: 77:14 Et dedúxit eos in nube diéi: * et tota nocte in illuminatióne ignis.
content.english: 77:14 And he conducted them with a cloud by day: * and all the night with a light of fire.

segments.t: Et dedúxit eos in nube diéi: * et tota nocte in illuminatióne ignis.

content.latin: 77:15 Interrúpit petram in erémo: * et adaquávit eos velut in abýsso multa.
content.english: 77:15 He struck the rock in the wilderness: * and gave them to drink, as out of the great deep.

segments.t: Interrúpit petram in erémo: * et adaquávit eos velut in abýsso multa.

content.latin: 77:16 Et edúxit aquam de petra: * et dedúxit tamquam flúmina aquas.
content.english: 77:16 He brought forth water out of the rock: * and made streams run down as rivers.

segments.t: Et edúxit aquam de petra: * et dedúxit tamquam flúmina aquas.

Psalmus 77(17-31)

content.latin: 77:17 Et apposuérunt adhuc peccáre ei: * in iram excitavérunt Excélsum in inaquóso.
content.english: 77:17 And they added yet more sin against him: * they provoked the most High to wrath in the place without water.

segments.t: Et apposuérunt adhuc peccáre ei: * in iram excitavérunt Excélsum in inaquóso.

content.latin: 77:18 Et tentavérunt Deum in córdibus suis, * ut péterent escas animábus suis.
content.english: 77:18 And they tempted God in their hearts, * by asking meat for their desires.

segments.t: Et tentavérunt Deum in córdibus suis, * ut péterent escas animábus suis.

content.latin: 77:19 Et male locúti sunt de Deo: * dixérunt: Numquid póterit Deus paráre mensam in desérto?
content.english: 77:19 And they spoke ill of God: * they said: Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?

segments.t: Et male locúti sunt de Deo: * dixérunt: Numquid póterit Deus paráre mensam in desérto?

content.latin: 77:20 Quóniam percússit petram, et fluxérunt aquæ: * et torréntes inundavérunt.
content.english: 77:20 Because he struck the rock, and the waters gushed out, * and the streams overflowed.

segments.t: Quóniam percússit petram, et fluxérunt aquæ: * et torréntes inundavérunt.

content.latin: 77:20 Numquid et panem póterit dare, * aut paráre mensam pópulo suo?
content.english: 77:20 Can he also give bread, * or provide a table for his people?

segments.t: Numquid et panem póterit dare, * aut paráre mensam pópulo suo?

content.latin: 77:21 Ídeo audívit Dóminus, et dístulit: * et ignis accénsus est in Iacob, et ira ascéndit in Israël.
content.english: 77:21 Therefore the Lord heard, and was angry: * and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath came up against Israel.

segments.t: Ídeo audívit Dóminus, et dístulit: * et ignis accénsus est in Iacob, et ira ascéndit in Israël.

content.latin: 77:22 Quia non credidérunt in Deo: * nec speravérunt in salutári eius:
content.english: 77:22 Because they believed not in God: * and trusted not in his salvation.

segments.t: Quia non credidérunt in Deo: * nec speravérunt in salutári eius:

content.latin: 77:23 Et mandávit núbibus désuper: * et iánuas cæli apéruit.
content.english: 77:23 And he had commanded the clouds from above, * and had opened the doors of heaven.

segments.t: Et mandávit núbibus désuper: * et iánuas cæli apéruit.

content.latin: 77:24 Et pluit illis manna ad manducándum: * et panem cæli dedit eis.
content.english: 77:24 And had rained down manna upon them to eat, * and had given them the bread of heaven.

segments.t: Et pluit illis manna ad manducándum: * et panem cæli dedit eis.

content.latin: 77:25 Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, * cibária misit eis in abundántia.
content.english: 77:25 Man ate the bread of angels: * he sent them provisions in abundance.

segments.t: Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, * cibária misit eis in abundántia.

content.latin: 77:26 Tránstulit Austrum de cælo: * et indúxit in virtúte sua Áfricum.
content.english: 77:26 He removed the south wind from heaven: * and by his power brought in the southwest wind.

segments.t: Tránstulit Austrum de cælo: * et indúxit in virtúte sua Áfricum.

content.latin: 77:27 Et pluit super eos sicut púlverem carnes: * et sicut arénam maris volatília pennáta.
content.english: 77:27 And he rained upon them flesh as dust: * and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.

segments.t: Et pluit super eos sicut púlverem carnes: * et sicut arénam maris volatília pennáta.

content.latin: 77:28 Et cecidérunt in médio castrórum eórum: * circa tabernácula eórum.
content.english: 77:28 And they fell in the midst of their camp, * round about their pavilions.

segments.t: Et cecidérunt in médio castrórum eórum: * circa tabernácula eórum.

content.latin: 77:29 Et manducavérunt, et saturáti sunt nimis, et desidérium eórum áttulit eis: * non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo.
content.english: 77:29 So they did eat, and were filled exceedingly, and he gave them their desire: * they were not defrauded of that which they craved.

segments.t: Et manducavérunt, et saturáti sunt nimis, et desidérium eórum áttulit eis: * non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo.

content.latin: 77:30 Adhuc escæ eórum erant in ore ipsórum: * et ira Dei ascéndit super eos.
content.english: 77:30 As yet their meat was in their mouth: * and the wrath of God came upon them.

segments.t: Adhuc escæ eórum erant in ore ipsórum: * et ira Dei ascéndit super eos.

content.latin: 77:31 Et occídit pingues eórum, * et eléctos Israël impedívit.
content.english: 77:31 And he slew the fat ones amongst them, * and brought down the chosen men of Israel.

segments.t: Et occídit pingues eórum, * et eléctos Israël impedívit.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.english: Ant. The Lord opened the doors of heaven and had rained down manna upon them to eat.

segments.t: Ant.
Iánuas cæli apéruit Dóminus, et pluit illis manna ad manducándum.

content.latin: Ant. Deus adiútor * est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.
content.english: Ant. God is their helper, * and the most high God their redeemer.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus adiútor * est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.

content.latin: 77:32 In ómnibus his peccavérunt adhuc: * et non credidérunt in mirabílibus eius.
content.english: 77:32 In all these things they sinned still: * and they believed not for his wondrous works.

segments.t: In ómnibus his peccavérunt adhuc: * et non credidérunt in mirabílibus eius.

content.latin: 77:33 Et defecérunt in vanitáte dies eórum: * et anni eórum cum festinatióne.
content.english: 77:33 And their days were consumed in vanity, * and their years in haste.

segments.t: Et defecérunt in vanitáte dies eórum: * et anni eórum cum festinatióne.

content.latin: 77:34 Cum occíderet eos, quærébant eum: * et revertebántur, et dilúculo veniébant ad eum.
content.english: 77:34 When he slew them, then they sought him: * and they returned, and came to him early in the morning.

segments.t: Cum occíderet eos, quærébant eum: * et revertebántur, et dilúculo veniébant ad eum.

content.latin: 77:35 Et rememoráti sunt quia Deus adiútor est eórum: * et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est.
content.english: 77:35 And they remembered that God was their helper: * and the most high God their redeemer.

segments.t: Et rememoráti sunt quia Deus adiútor est eórum: * et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est.

content.latin: 77:36 Et dilexérunt eum in ore suo, * et lingua sua mentíti sunt ei.
content.english: 77:36 And they loved him with their mouth: * and with their tongue they lied unto him:

segments.t: Et dilexérunt eum in ore suo, * et lingua sua mentíti sunt ei.

content.latin: 77:37 Cor autem eórum non erat rectum cum eo: * nec fidéles hábiti sunt in testaménto eius.
content.english: 77:37 But their heart was not right with him: * nor were they counted faithful in his covenant.

segments.t: Cor autem eórum non erat rectum cum eo: * nec fidéles hábiti sunt in testaménto eius.

content.latin: 77:38 Ipse autem est miséricors, et propítius fiet peccátis eórum: * et non dispérdet eos.
content.english: 77:38 But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: * and will not destroy them.

segments.t: Ipse autem est miséricors, et propítius fiet peccátis eórum: * et non dispérdet eos.

content.latin: 77:38 Et abundávit ut avérteret iram suam: * et non accéndit omnem iram suam:
content.english: 77:38 And many a time did he turn away his anger: * and did not kindle all his wrath.

segments.t: Et abundávit ut avérteret iram suam: * et non accéndit omnem iram suam:

content.latin: 77:39 Et recordátus est quia caro sunt: * spíritus vadens et non rédiens.
content.english: 77:39 And he remembered that they are flesh: * a wind that goeth and returneth not.

segments.t: Et recordátus est quia caro sunt: * spíritus vadens et non rédiens.

content.latin: 77:40 Quóties exacerbavérunt eum in desérto, * in iram concitavérunt eum in inaquóso?
content.english: 77:40 How often did they provoke him in the desert: * and move him to wrath in the place without water?

segments.t: Quóties exacerbavérunt eum in desérto, * in iram concitavérunt eum in inaquóso?

content.latin: 77:41 Et convérsi sunt, et tentavérunt Deum: * et Sanctum Israël exacerbavérunt.
content.english: 77:41 And they turned back and tempted God: * and grieved the holy one of Israel.

segments.t: Et convérsi sunt, et tentavérunt Deum: * et Sanctum Israël exacerbavérunt.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Deus adiútor est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.
content.english: Ant. God is their helper, and the most high God their redeemer.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus adiútor est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.

content.latin: Ant. Redémit eos * Dóminus de manu tribulántis.
content.english: Ant. The Lord redeemed them * from the hand of him that afflicted them.

segments.t: Ant.
Redémit eos * Dóminus de manu tribulántis.
Psalmus 77(42-58)

content.latin: 77:42 Non sunt recordáti manus eius, * die qua redémit eos de manu tribulántis.
content.english: 77:42 They remembered not his hand, * in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them:

segments.t: Non sunt recordáti manus eius, * die qua redémit eos de manu tribulántis.

content.latin: 77:43 Sicut pósuit in Ægýpto signa sua, * et prodígia sua in campo Táneos.
content.english: 77:43 How he wrought his signs in Egypt, * and his wonders in the field of Tanis.

segments.t: Sicut pósuit in Ægýpto signa sua, * et prodígia sua in campo Táneos.

content.latin: 77:44 Et convértit in sánguinem flúmina eórum: * et imbres eórum, ne bíberent.
content.english: 77:44 And he turned their rivers into blood, * and their showers that they might not drink.

segments.t: Et convértit in sánguinem flúmina eórum: * et imbres eórum, ne bíberent.

content.latin: 77:45 Misit in eos cœnomyíam, et comédit eos: * et ranam, et dispérdidit eos.
content.english: 77:45 He sent amongst them diverse sorts of flies, which devoured them: * and frogs which destroyed them.

segments.t: Misit in eos cœnomyíam, et comédit eos: * et ranam, et dispérdidit eos.

content.latin: 77:46 Et dedit ærúgini fructus eórum: * et labóres eórum locústæ.
content.english: 77:46 And he gave up their fruits to the blast, * and their labours to the locust.

segments.t: Et dedit ærúgini fructus eórum: * et labóres eórum locústæ.

content.latin: 77:47 Et occídit in grándine víneas eórum: * et moros eórum in pruína.
content.english: 77:47 And he destroyed their vineyards with hail, * and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.

segments.t: Et occídit in grándine víneas eórum: * et moros eórum in pruína.

content.latin: 77:48 Et trádidit grándini iuménta eórum: * et possessiónem eórum igni.
content.english: 77:48 And he gave up their cattle to the hail, * and their stock to the fire.

segments.t: Et trádidit grándini iuménta eórum: * et possessiónem eórum igni.

content.latin: 77:49 Misit in eos iram indignatiónis suæ: * indignatiónem, et iram, et tribulatiónem: immissiónes per ángelos malos.
content.english: 77:49 And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: * indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels.

segments.t: Misit in eos iram indignatiónis suæ: * indignatiónem, et iram, et tribulatiónem: immissiónes per ángelos malos.

content.latin: 77:50 Viam fecit sémitæ iræ suæ, non pepércit a morte animábus eórum: * et iuménta eórum in morte conclúsit.
content.english: 77:50 He made a way for a path to his anger: * he spared not their souls from death, and their cattle he shut up in death.

segments.t: Viam fecit sémitæ iræ suæ, non pepércit a morte animábus eórum: * et iuménta eórum in morte conclúsit.

content.latin: 77:51 Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra Ægýpti: * primítias omnis labóris eórum in tabernáculis Cham.
content.english: 77:51 And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt: * the firstfruits of all their labour in the tabernacles of Cham.

segments.t: Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra Ægýpti: * primítias omnis labóris eórum in tabernáculis Cham.

content.latin: 77:52 Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum: * et perdúxit eos tamquam gregem in desérto.
content.english: 77:52 And he took away his own people as sheep: * and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.

segments.t: Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum: * et perdúxit eos tamquam gregem in desérto.

content.latin: 77:53 Et dedúxit eos in spe, et non timuérunt: * et inimícos eórum opéruit mare.
content.english: 77:53 And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: * and the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

segments.t: Et dedúxit eos in spe, et non timuérunt: * et inimícos eórum opéruit mare.

content.latin: 77:54 Et indúxit eos in montem sanctificatiónis suæ: * montem, quem acquisívit déxtera eius.
content.english: 77:54 And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: * the mountain which his right hand had purchased.

segments.t: Et indúxit eos in montem sanctificatiónis suæ: * montem, quem acquisívit déxtera eius.

content.latin: 77:54 Et eiécit a fácie eórum gentes: * et sorte divísit eis terram in funículo distributiónis.
content.english: 77:54 And he cast out the Gentiles before them: * and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution.

segments.t: Et eiécit a fácie eórum gentes: * et sorte divísit eis terram in funículo distributiónis.

content.latin: 77:55 Et habitáre fecit in tabernáculis eórum: * tribus Israël.
content.english: 77:55 And he made the tribes of Israel * to dwell in their tabernacles.

segments.t: Et habitáre fecit in tabernáculis eórum: * tribus Israël.

content.latin: 77:56 Et tentavérunt, et exacerbavérunt Deum excélsum: * et testimónia eius non custodiérunt.
content.english: 77:56 Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God: * and they kept not his testimonies.

segments.t: Et tentavérunt, et exacerbavérunt Deum excélsum: * et testimónia eius non custodiérunt.

content.latin: 77:57 Et avertérunt se, et non servavérunt pactum: * quemádmodum patres eórum convérsi sunt in arcum pravum.
content.english: 77:57 And they turned away, and kept not the covenant: * even like their fathers they were turned aside as a crooked bow.

segments.t: Et avertérunt se, et non servavérunt pactum: * quemádmodum patres eórum convérsi sunt in arcum pravum.

content.latin: 77:58 In iram concitavérunt eum in cóllibus suis: * et in sculptílibus suis ad æmulatiónem eum provocavérunt.
content.english: 77:58 They provoked him to anger on their hills: * and moved him to jealousy with their graven things.

segments.t: In iram concitavérunt eum in cóllibus suis: * et in sculptílibus suis ad æmulatiónem eum provocavérunt.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Redémit eos Dóminus de manu tribulántis.
content.english: Ant. The Lord redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them.

segments.t: Ant.
Redémit eos Dóminus de manu tribulántis.

content.latin: Ant. Ædificávit * Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.
content.english: Ant. God built * his sanctuary in the earth.

segments.t: Ant.
Ædificávit * Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.
Psalmus 77(59-72)

content.latin: 77:59 Audívit Deus, et sprevit: * et ad níhilum redégit valde Israël.
content.english: 77:59 God heard, and despised them, * and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing.

segments.t: Audívit Deus, et sprevit: * et ad níhilum redégit valde Israël.

content.latin: 77:60 Et répulit tabernáculum Silo: * tabernáculum suum, ubi habitávit in homínibus.
content.english: 77:60 And he put away the tabernacle of Silo, * his tabernacle where he dwelt among men.

segments.t: Et répulit tabernáculum Silo: * tabernáculum suum, ubi habitávit in homínibus.

content.latin: 77:61 Et trádidit in captivitátem virtútem eórum: * et pulchritúdinem eórum in manus inimíci.
content.english: 77:61 And he delivered their strength into captivity: * and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.

segments.t: Et trádidit in captivitátem virtútem eórum: * et pulchritúdinem eórum in manus inimíci.

content.latin: 77:62 Et conclúsit in gládio pópulum suum: * et hereditátem suam sprevit.
content.english: 77:62 And he shut up his people under the sword: * and he despised his inheritance.

segments.t: Et conclúsit in gládio pópulum suum: * et hereditátem suam sprevit.

content.latin: 77:63 Iúvenes eórum comédit ignis: * et vírgines eórum non sunt lamentátæ.
content.english: 77:63 Fire consumed their young men: * and their maidens were not lamented.

segments.t: Iúvenes eórum comédit ignis: * et vírgines eórum non sunt lamentátæ.

content.latin: 77:64 Sacerdótes eórum in gládio cecidérunt: * et víduæ eórum non plorabántur.
content.english: 77:64 Their priests fell by the sword: * and their widows did not mourn.

segments.t: Sacerdótes eórum in gládio cecidérunt: * et víduæ eórum non plorabántur.

content.latin: 77:65 Et excitátus est tamquam dórmiens Dóminus: * tamquam potens crapulátus a vino.
content.english: 77:65 And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, * and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine.

segments.t: Et excitátus est tamquam dórmiens Dóminus: * tamquam potens crapulátus a vino.

content.latin: 77:66 Et percússit inimícos suos in posterióra: * oppróbrium sempitérnum dedit illis.
content.english: 77:66 And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts: * he put them to an everlasting reproach.

segments.t: Et percússit inimícos suos in posterióra: * oppróbrium sempitérnum dedit illis.

content.latin: 77:67 Et répulit tabernáculum Ioseph: * et tribum Éphraim non elégit.
content.english: 77:67 And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: * and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:

segments.t: Et répulit tabernáculum Ioseph: * et tribum Éphraim non elégit.

content.latin: 77:68 Sed elégit tribum Iuda, * montem Sion quem diléxit.
content.english: 77:68 But he chose the tribe of Juda, * mount Sion which he loved.

segments.t: Sed elégit tribum Iuda, * montem Sion quem diléxit.

content.latin: 77:69 Et ædificávit sicut unicórnium sanctifícium suum in terra, * quam fundávit in sǽcula.
content.english: 77:69 And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns, in the land * which he founded for ever.

segments.t: Et ædificávit sicut unicórnium sanctifícium suum in terra, * quam fundávit in sǽcula.

content.latin: 77:70 Et elégit David, servum suum, et sústulit eum de grégibus óvium: * de post fœtántes accépit eum,
content.english: 77:70 And he chose his servant David, and took him from the flocks of sheep: * he brought him from following the ewes great with young,

segments.t: Et elégit David, servum suum, et sústulit eum de grégibus óvium: * de post fœtántes accépit eum,

content.latin: 77:71 Páscere Iacob, servum suum, * et Israël, hereditátem suam:
content.english: 77:71 To feed Jacob his servant, * and Israel his inheritance.

segments.t: Páscere Iacob, servum suum, * et Israël, hereditátem suam:

content.latin: 77:72 Et pavit eos in innocéntia cordis sui: * et in intelléctibus mánuum suárum dedúxit eos.
content.english: 77:72 And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: * and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands.

segments.t: Et pavit eos in innocéntia cordis sui: * et in intelléctibus mánuum suárum dedúxit eos.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ædificávit Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.
content.english: Ant. God built his sanctuary in the earth.

segments.t: Ant.
Ædificávit Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.

content.latin: Ant. Ádiuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris.
content.english: Ant. Help us, O God, our Saviour, * deliver us: and forgive us our sins.

segments.t: Ant.
Ádiuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris.

content.latin: Psalmus 78 [7]
content.english: Psalm 78 [7]

segments.t: Psalmus 78

content.latin: 78:1 Deus, venérunt gentes in hereditátem tuam, polluérunt templum sanctum tuum: * posuérunt Ierúsalem in pomórum custódiam.
content.english: 78:1 O God, the heathens are come into thy inheritance, they have defiled thy holy temple: * they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit.

segments.t: Deus, venérunt gentes in hereditátem tuam, polluérunt templum sanctum tuum: * posuérunt Ierúsalem in pomórum custódiam.

content.latin: 78:2 Posuérunt morticína servórum tuórum, escas volatílibus cæli: * carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.
content.english: 78:2 They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: * the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth.

segments.t: Posuérunt morticína servórum tuórum, escas volatílibus cæli: * carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.

content.latin: 78:3 Effudérunt sánguinem eórum tamquam aquam in circúitu Ierúsalem: * et non erat qui sepelíret.
content.english: 78:3 They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem, * and there was none to bury them.

segments.t: Effudérunt sánguinem eórum tamquam aquam in circúitu Ierúsalem: * et non erat qui sepelíret.

content.latin: 78:4 Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris: * subsannátio et illúsio his, qui in circúitu nostro sunt.
content.english: 78:4 We are become a reproach to our neighbours: * a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.

segments.t: Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris: * subsannátio et illúsio his, qui in circúitu nostro sunt.

content.latin: 78:5 Úsquequo, Dómine, irascéris in finem: * accendétur velut ignis zelus tuus?
content.english: 78:5 How long, O Lord, wilt thou be angry for ever: * shall thy zeal be kindled like a fire?

segments.t: Úsquequo, Dómine, irascéris in finem: * accendétur velut ignis zelus tuus?

content.latin: 78:6 Effúnde iram tuam in gentes, quæ te non novérunt: * et in regna quæ nomen tuum non invocavérunt:
content.english: 78:6 Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that have not known thee: * and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.

segments.t: Effúnde iram tuam in gentes, quæ te non novérunt: * et in regna quæ nomen tuum non invocavérunt:

content.latin: 78:7 Quia comedérunt Iacob: * et locum eius desolavérunt.
content.english: 78:7 Because they have devoured Jacob; * and have laid waste his place.

segments.t: Quia comedérunt Iacob: * et locum eius desolavérunt.

content.latin: 78:8 Ne memíneris iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum, cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ: * quia páuperes facti sumus nimis.
content.english: 78:8 Remember not our former iniquities: let thy mercies speedily prevent us, * for we are become exceeding poor.

segments.t: Ne memíneris iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum, cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ: * quia páuperes facti sumus nimis.

content.latin: 78:9 Ádiuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos: * et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter nomen tuum:
content.english: 78:9 Help us, O God, our saviour: and for the glory of thy name, O Lord, deliver us: * and forgive us our sins for thy name’s sake:

segments.t: Ádiuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos: * et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter nomen tuum:

content.latin: 78:10 Ne forte dicant in géntibus: Ubi est Deus eórum? * et innotéscat in natiónibus coram óculis nostris.
content.english: 78:10 Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God? * And let him be made known among the nations before our eyes,

segments.t: Ne forte dicant in géntibus: Ubi est Deus eórum? * et innotéscat in natiónibus coram óculis nostris.

content.latin: 78:10 Últio sánguinis servórum tuórum, qui effúsus est: * intróeat in conspéctu tuo gémitus compeditórum.
content.english: 78:10 By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed: * let the sighing of the prisoners come in before thee.

segments.t: Últio sánguinis servórum tuórum, qui effúsus est: * intróeat in conspéctu tuo gémitus compeditórum.

content.latin: 78:11 Secúndum magnitúdinem brácchii tui, * pósside fílios mortificatórum.
content.english: 78:11 According to the greatness of thy arm, * take possession of the children of them that have been put to death.

segments.t: Secúndum magnitúdinem brácchii tui, * pósside fílios mortificatórum.

content.latin: 78:12 Et redde vicínis nostris séptuplum in sinu eórum: * impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine.
content.english: 78:12 And render to our neighbours sevenfold in their bosom: * the reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Et redde vicínis nostris séptuplum in sinu eórum: * impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine.

content.latin: 78:13 Nos autem pópulus tuus, et oves páscuæ tuæ, * confitébimur tibi in sǽculum.
content.english: 78:13 But we thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture, * will give thanks to thee for ever.

segments.t: Nos autem pópulus tuus, et oves páscuæ tuæ, * confitébimur tibi in sǽculum.

content.latin: 78:13 In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábimus laudem tuam.
content.english: 78:13 We will shew forth thy praise, * unto generation and generation.

segments.t: In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábimus laudem tuam.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Cum audíeris mulíerem illam dicéntem: Beátus venter qui te portávit, et úbera quæ tu suxísti; deínde Dóminum respondéntem: Quinímmo beáti qui áudiunt verbum Dei et custódiunt illud; ea senténtia dictum exístima, non quod Matrem neglégeret, sed nihil ei utilitátis matris nomen allatúrum osténderet, nisi bonitáte et fide præstáret. Quod si Maríæ nihil, sine virtúte, matérna cáritas erat profutúra; longe minus nobis patris, fratris, matris, fílii bónitas, nisi áliquid nostrum afferámus.
content.english: When you give ear to the saying of that woman: Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which thou hast sucked: and to the Lord's reply: Yea, rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God and keep it: think not that he made this observation as slighting his Mother, but as wishing to shew that it would profit her nothing to be called his Mother, unless she excelled in goodness and faith. Now, if a mother's love would avail Mary nothing without virtue, much less will it avail us to be a good father, brother, mother, or son, unless we are good in ourselves.

content.latin: In nullo namque álio, nisi in solis sui ipsíus virtútibus, post divínam grátiam, de salúte cuípiam sperándum est. Nam, si id profutúrum erat per se Maríæ, profuísset étiam Iudǽis, quorum consanguíneus Christus secúndum carnem; profuísset civitáti, in qua natus est; profuísset frátribus. Atqui, dum fratres rerum suárum curam habuérunt, nihil eis propinquitátis nomen prófuit, sed cum réliquo mundo damnáti erant.
content.english: For indeed, salvation for anyone, apart from the divine grace, is to be hoped for in nothing else but his own virtues. For if her kinship in itself could have profited Mary, it would also have profited the Jews, for Christ was their kinsman according to the flesh; it would have profited the city in which he was born; it would have profited his brethren. Yet as long as his brethren cared only for their own interests, their relationship to Christ profited them nothing, but they were condemned with the rest of the world.

content.latin: Tunc autem admiratióni esse cœpérunt, quando própria claruérunt virtúte. Pátria vero nihil inde consecúta cécidit, et incéndio absúmpta est; concíves mísere interémpti periére; consanguínei secúndum carnem nil ad salútem lucráti sunt, deficiénte virtútis patrocínio. Verum Apóstoli ante omnes claríssimi evasérunt, cum se ad veram et expeténdam eius familiaritátem consuetudinémque per obediéntiam contulérunt. Hinc intellégimus, fide semper nobis opus esse, et vita quæ virtútibus lúceat: hæc dumtáxat salvos nos fácere póterit.
content.english: Then only did they begin to be worthy of admiration, when they shone by their own virtue. His native land, indeed, having gained nothing from its own connection with him, fell and was burnt by fire; his fellow-citizens were put to death and perished miserably; his kindred according to the flesh gained nothing towards their salvation; insofar as all these lacked the protection of virtue. But of them all, the Apostles became the most renowned, since by obedience they joined themselves to him in a right and desirable friendship and companionship. From this we learn, that we always have need of faith, and a life shining with virtues; since this alone will have power to save us.

content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Deus, qui virginálem aulam beátæ Maríæ, in qua habitáres, elígere dignátus es: da, quǽsumus; ut, sua nos defensióne munítos, iucúndos fácias suæ interésse festivitáti:
content.english: O God, Who wast pleased to choose for thy dwelling-place the maiden palace of Blessed Mary, grant, we beseech thee, that her protection may shield us, and make us glad in her commemoration.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.latin: Psalmus 50 [1]
content.english: Psalm 50 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 50

content.latin: 50:3 Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 50:3 Have mercy on me, O God, * according to thy great mercy.

segments.t: Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.

content.latin: 50:3 Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.
content.english: 50:3 And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies * blot out my iniquity.

segments.t: Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.

content.latin: 50:4 Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.
content.english: 50:4 Wash me yet more from my iniquity, * and cleanse me from my sin.

segments.t: Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.

content.latin: 50:5 Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
content.english: 50:5 For I know my iniquity, * and my sin is always before me.

segments.t: Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.

content.latin: 50:6 Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut iustificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum iudicáris.
content.english: 50:6 To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: * that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.

segments.t: Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut iustificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum iudicáris.

content.latin: 50:7 Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
content.english: 50:7 For behold I was conceived in iniquities; * and in sins did my mother conceive me.

segments.t: Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.

content.latin: 50:8 Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
content.english: 50:8 For behold thou hast loved truth: * the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.

segments.t: Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.

content.latin: 50:9 Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
content.english: 50:9 Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: * thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

segments.t: Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.

content.latin: 50:10 Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
content.english: 50:10 To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: * and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

segments.t: Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.

content.latin: 50:11 Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
content.english: 50:11 Turn away thy face from my sins, * and blot out all my iniquities.

segments.t: Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.

content.latin: 50:12 Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
content.english: 50:12 Create a clean heart in me, O God: * and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

segments.t: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.

content.latin: 50:13 Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
content.english: 50:13 Cast me not away from thy face; * and take not thy holy spirit from me.

segments.t: Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.

content.latin: 50:14 Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.
content.english: 50:14 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, * and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

segments.t: Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.

content.latin: 50:15 Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.
content.english: 50:15 I will teach the unjust thy ways: * and the wicked shall be converted to thee.

segments.t: Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.

content.latin: 50:16 Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea iustítiam tuam.
content.english: 50:16 Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: * and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

segments.t: Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea iustítiam tuam.

content.latin: 50:17 Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: 50:17 O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: * and my mouth shall declare thy praise.

segments.t: Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.

content.latin: 50:18 Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.
content.english: 50:18 For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: * with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.

segments.t: Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.

content.latin: 50:19 Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
content.english: 50:19 A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: * a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

segments.t: Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.

content.latin: 50:20 Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Ierúsalem.
content.english: 50:20 Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; * that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

segments.t: Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 50:21 Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium iustítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
content.english: 50:21 Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: * then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.

segments.t: Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium iustítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Cor contrítum et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
content.english: Ant. A contrite and a humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

segments.t: Ant.
Cor contrítum et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.

content.latin: Ant. Propter nomen tuum, * Dómine, vivificábis me in æquitáte tua.
content.english: Ant. For thy name's sake, * O Lord, thou wilt quicken me in thy justice.

segments.t: Ant.
Propter nomen tuum, * Dómine, vivificábis me in æquitáte tua.

content.latin: Psalmus 142 [2]
content.english: Psalm 142 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 142

content.latin: 142:1 Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: áuribus pércipe obsecratiónem meam in veritáte tua: * exáudi me in tua iustítia.
content.english: 142:1 Hear, O Lord, my prayer: give ear to my supplication in thy truth: * hear me in thy justice.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: áuribus pércipe obsecratiónem meam in veritáte tua: * exáudi me in tua iustítia.

content.latin: 142:2 Et non intres in iudícium cum servo tuo: * quia non iustificábitur in conspéctu tuo omnis vivens.
content.english: 142:2 And enter not into judgment with thy servant: * for in thy sight no man living shall be justified.

segments.t: Et non intres in iudícium cum servo tuo: * quia non iustificábitur in conspéctu tuo omnis vivens.

content.latin: 142:3 Quia persecútus est inimícus ánimam meam: * humiliávit in terra vitam meam.
content.english: 142:3 For the enemy hath persecuted my soul: * he hath brought down my life to the earth.

segments.t: Quia persecútus est inimícus ánimam meam: * humiliávit in terra vitam meam.

content.latin: 142:3 Collocávit me in obscúris sicut mórtuos sǽculi: * et anxiátus est super me spíritus meus, in me turbátum est cor meum.
content.english: 142:3 He hath made me to dwell in darkness as those that have been dead of old: * and my spirit is in anguish within me: my heart within me is troubled.

segments.t: Collocávit me in obscúris sicut mórtuos sǽculi: * et anxiátus est super me spíritus meus, in me turbátum est cor meum.

content.latin: 142:5 Memor fui diérum antiquórum, meditátus sum in ómnibus opéribus tuis: * in factis mánuum tuárum meditábar.
content.english: 142:5 I remembered the days of old, I meditated on all thy works: * I meditated upon the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Memor fui diérum antiquórum, meditátus sum in ómnibus opéribus tuis: * in factis mánuum tuárum meditábar.

content.latin: 142:6 Expándi manus meas ad te: * ánima mea sicut terra sine aqua tibi.
content.english: 142:6 I stretched forth my hands to thee: * my soul is as earth without water unto thee.

segments.t: Expándi manus meas ad te: * ánima mea sicut terra sine aqua tibi.

content.latin: 142:7 Velóciter exáudi me, Dómine: * defécit spíritus meus.
content.english: 142:7 Hear me speedily, O Lord: * my spirit hath fainted away.

segments.t: Velóciter exáudi me, Dómine: * defécit spíritus meus.

content.latin: 142:7 Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * et símilis ero descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 142:7 Turn not away thy face from me, * lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.

segments.t: Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * et símilis ero descendéntibus in lacum.

content.latin: 142:8 Audítam fac mihi mane misericórdiam tuam: * quia in te sperávi.
content.english: 142:8 Cause me to hear thy mercy in the morning; * for in thee have I hoped.

segments.t: Audítam fac mihi mane misericórdiam tuam: * quia in te sperávi.

content.latin: 142:8 Notam fac mihi viam, in qua ámbulem: * quia ad te levávi ánimam meam.
content.english: 142:8 Make the way known to me, wherein I should walk: * for I have lifted up my soul to thee.

segments.t: Notam fac mihi viam, in qua ámbulem: * quia ad te levávi ánimam meam.

content.latin: 142:9 Éripe me de inimícis meis, Dómine, ad te confúgi: * doce me fácere voluntátem tuam, quia Deus meus es tu.
content.english: 142:9 Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord, to thee have I fled: * teach me to do thy will, for thou art my God.

segments.t: Éripe me de inimícis meis, Dómine, ad te confúgi: * doce me fácere voluntátem tuam, quia Deus meus es tu.

content.latin: 142:10 Spíritus tuus bonus dedúcet me in terram rectam: * propter nomen tuum, Dómine, vivificábis me, in æquitáte tua.
content.english: 142:10 Thy good spirit shall lead me into the right land: * for thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt quicken me in thy justice.

segments.t: Spíritus tuus bonus dedúcet me in terram rectam: * propter nomen tuum, Dómine, vivificábis me, in æquitáte tua.

content.latin: 142:11 Edúces de tribulatióne ánimam meam: * et in misericórdia tua dispérdes inimícos meos.
content.english: 142:11 Thou wilt bring my soul out of trouble: * and in thy mercy thou wilt destroy my enemies.

segments.t: Edúces de tribulatióne ánimam meam: * et in misericórdia tua dispérdes inimícos meos.

content.latin: 142:12 Et perdes omnes, qui tríbulant ánimam meam: * quóniam ego servus tuus sum.
content.english: 142:12 And thou wilt cut off all them that afflict my soul: * for I am thy servant.

segments.t: Et perdes omnes, qui tríbulant ánimam meam: * quóniam ego servus tuus sum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, vivificábis me in æquitáte tua.
content.english: Ant. For thy name's sake, O Lord, thou wilt quicken me in thy justice.

segments.t: Ant.
Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, vivificábis me in æquitáte tua.

content.latin: Ant. Deus, tu convérsus * vivificábis nos, et plebs tua lætábitur in te.
content.english: Ant. Thou wilt turn, O God, * Thou wilt quicken us and bring us to life.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus, tu convérsus * vivificábis nos, et plebs tua lætábitur in te.

content.latin: Psalmus 84 [3]
content.english: Psalm 84 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 84

content.latin: 84:2 Benedixísti, Dómine, terram tuam: * avertísti captivitátem Iacob.
content.english: 84:2 Lord, thou hast blessed thy land: * thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob.

segments.t: Benedixísti, Dómine, terram tuam: * avertísti captivitátem Iacob.

content.latin: 84:3 Remisísti iniquitátem plebis tuæ: * operuísti ómnia peccáta eórum.
content.english: 84:3 Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people: * thou hast covered all their sins.

segments.t: Remisísti iniquitátem plebis tuæ: * operuísti ómnia peccáta eórum.

content.latin: 84:4 Mitigásti omnem iram tuam: * avertísti ab ira indignatiónis tuæ.
content.english: 84:4 Thou hast mitigated all thy anger: * thou hast turned away from the wrath of thy indignation.

segments.t: Mitigásti omnem iram tuam: * avertísti ab ira indignatiónis tuæ.

content.latin: 84:5 Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster: * et avérte iram tuam a nobis.
content.english: 84:5 Convert us, O God our saviour: * and turn off thy anger from us.

segments.t: Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster: * et avérte iram tuam a nobis.

content.latin: 84:6 Numquid in ætérnum irascéris nobis? * aut exténdes iram tuam a generatióne in generatiónem?
content.english: 84:6 Wilt thou be angry with us for ever: * or wilt thou extend thy wrath from generation to generation?

segments.t: Numquid in ætérnum irascéris nobis? * aut exténdes iram tuam a generatióne in generatiónem?

content.latin: 84:7 Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos: * et plebs tua lætábitur in te.
content.english: 84:7 Thou wilt turn, O God, and bring us to life: * and thy people shall rejoice in thee.

segments.t: Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos: * et plebs tua lætábitur in te.

content.latin: 84:8 Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam: * et salutáre tuum da nobis.
content.english: 84:8 Shew us, O Lord, thy mercy; * and grant us thy salvation.

segments.t: Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam: * et salutáre tuum da nobis.

content.latin: 84:9 Áudiam quid loquátur in me Dóminus Deus: * quóniam loquétur pacem in plebem suam.
content.english: 84:9 I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me: * for he will speak peace

segments.t: Áudiam quid loquátur in me Dóminus Deus: * quóniam loquétur pacem in plebem suam.

content.latin: 84:9 Et super sanctos suos: * et in eos, qui convertúntur ad cor.
content.english: 84:9 And unto his saints: * and unto them that are converted to the heart.

segments.t: Et super sanctos suos: * et in eos, qui convertúntur ad cor.

content.latin: 84:10 Verúmtamen prope timéntes eum salutáre ipsíus: * ut inhábitet glória in terra nostra.
content.english: 84:10 Surely his salvation is near to them that fear him: * that glory may dwell in our land.

segments.t: Verúmtamen prope timéntes eum salutáre ipsíus: * ut inhábitet glória in terra nostra.

content.latin: 84:11 Misericórdia, et véritas obviavérunt sibi: * iustítia, et pax osculátæ sunt.
content.english: 84:11 Mercy and truth have met each other: * justice and peace have kissed.

segments.t: Misericórdia, et véritas obviavérunt sibi: * iustítia, et pax osculátæ sunt.

content.latin: 84:12 Véritas de terra orta est: * et iustítia de cælo prospéxit.
content.english: 84:12 Truth is sprung out of the earth: * and justice hath looked down from heaven.

segments.t: Véritas de terra orta est: * et iustítia de cælo prospéxit.

content.latin: 84:13 Étenim Dóminus dabit benignitátem: * et terra nostra dabit fructum suum.
content.english: 84:13 For the Lord will give goodness: * and our earth shall yield her fruit.

segments.t: Étenim Dóminus dabit benignitátem: * et terra nostra dabit fructum suum.

content.latin: 84:14 Iustítia ante eum ambulábit: * et ponet in via gressus suos.
content.english: 84:14 Justice shall walk before him: * and shall set his steps in the way.

segments.t: Iustítia ante eum ambulábit: * et ponet in via gressus suos.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos, et plebs tua lætábitur in te.
content.english: Ant. Thou wilt turn, O God, Thou wilt quicken us and bring us to life.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos, et plebs tua lætábitur in te.

content.latin: Ant. Cum irátus fúeris, * Dómine, misericórdiæ recordáberis.
content.english: Ant. When thou art angry, * O Lord, thou wilt remember mercy.

segments.t: Ant.
Cum irátus fúeris, * Dómine, misericórdiæ recordáberis.

content.latin: Canticum Habacuc [4]
content.english: Canticle of Habacuc [4]

segments.t: Canticum Habacuc

content.latin: 3:2 Dómine, audívi auditiónem tuam, * et tímui.
content.english: 3:2 O Lord, I have heard thy hearing, * and was afraid.

segments.t: Dómine, audívi auditiónem tuam, * et tímui.

content.latin: 3:3 Dómine, opus tuum, * in médio annórum vivífica illud:
content.english: 3:3 O Lord, thy work, * in the midst of the years bring it to life:

segments.t: Dómine, opus tuum, * in médio annórum vivífica illud:

content.latin: 3:4 In médio annórum notum fácies: * cum irátus fúeris, misericórdiæ recordáberis.
content.english: 3:4 In the midst of the years thou shalt make it known: * when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy.

segments.t: In médio annórum notum fácies: * cum irátus fúeris, misericórdiæ recordáberis.

content.latin: 3:5 Deus ab Austro véniet, * et sanctus de monte Pharan:
content.english: 3:5 God will come from the south, * and the holy one from mount Pharan:

segments.t: Deus ab Austro véniet, * et sanctus de monte Pharan:

content.latin: 3:6 Opéruit cælos glória eius: * et laudis eius plena est terra.
content.english: 3:6 His glory covered the heavens, * and the earth is full of his praise.

segments.t: Opéruit cælos glória eius: * et laudis eius plena est terra.

content.latin: 3:7 Splendor eius ut lux erit: * córnua in mánibus eius:
content.english: 3:7 His brightness shall be as the light: * horns are in his hands:

segments.t: Splendor eius ut lux erit: * córnua in mánibus eius:

content.latin: 3:8 Ibi abscóndita est fortitúdo eius: * ante fáciem eius ibit mors.
content.english: 3:8 There is his strength hid: * Death shall go before his face.

segments.t: Ibi abscóndita est fortitúdo eius: * ante fáciem eius ibit mors.

content.latin: 3:9 Et egrediétur diábolus ante pedes eius. * Stetit, et mensus est terram.
content.english: 3:9 And the devil shall go forth before his feet. * He stood and measured the earth.

segments.t: Et egrediétur diábolus ante pedes eius. * Stetit, et mensus est terram.

content.latin: 3:10 Aspéxit, et dissólvit gentes: * et contríti sunt montes sǽculi.
content.english: 3:10 He beheld, and melted the nations: * and the ancient mountains were crushed to pieces.

segments.t: Aspéxit, et dissólvit gentes: * et contríti sunt montes sǽculi.

content.latin: 3:11 Incurváti sunt colles mundi, * ab itinéribus æternitátis eius.
content.english: 3:11 The hills of the world were bowed down * by the journeys of his eternity.

segments.t: Incurváti sunt colles mundi, * ab itinéribus æternitátis eius.

content.latin: 3:12 Pro iniquitáte vidi tentória Æthiópiæ, * turbabúntur pelles terræ Mádian.
content.english: 3:12 I saw the tents of Ethiopia for their iniquity, * the curtains of the land of Madian shall be troubled.

segments.t: Pro iniquitáte vidi tentória Æthiópiæ, * turbabúntur pelles terræ Mádian.

content.latin: 3:13 Numquid in flumínibus irátus es, Dómine? * aut in flumínibus furor tuus? vel in mari indignátio tua?
content.english: 3:13 Wast thou angry, O Lord, with the rivers? * or was thy wrath upon the rivers? or thy indignation in the sea?

segments.t: Numquid in flumínibus irátus es, Dómine? * aut in flumínibus furor tuus? vel in mari indignátio tua?

content.latin: 3:14 Qui ascéndes super equos tuos: * et quadrígæ tuæ salvátio.
content.english: 3:14 Who will ride upon thy horses: * and thy chariots are salvation.

segments.t: Qui ascéndes super equos tuos: * et quadrígæ tuæ salvátio.

content.latin: 3:15 Súscitans suscitábis arcum tuum: * iuraménta tríbubus quæ locútus es.
content.english: 3:15 Thou wilt surely take up thy bow: * according to the oaths which thou hast spoken to the tribes.

segments.t: Súscitans suscitábis arcum tuum: * iuraménta tríbubus quæ locútus es.

content.latin: 3:16 Flúvios scindes terræ: vidérunt te, et doluérunt montes: * gurges aquárum tránsiit.
content.english: 3:16 Thou wilt divide the rivers of the earth. The mountains saw thee, and were grieved: * the great body of waters passed away.

segments.t: Flúvios scindes terræ: vidérunt te, et doluérunt montes: * gurges aquárum tránsiit.

content.latin: 3:17 Dedit abýssus vocem suam: * altitúdo manus suas levávit.
content.english: 3:17 The deep put forth its voice: * the deep lifted up its hands.

segments.t: Dedit abýssus vocem suam: * altitúdo manus suas levávit.

content.latin: 3:18 Sol, et luna stetérunt in habitáculo suo, * in luce sagittárum tuárum, ibunt in splendóre fulgurántis hastæ tuæ.
content.english: 3:18 The sun and the moon stood still in their habitation, * in the light of thy arrows, they shall go in the brightness of thy glittering spear.

segments.t: Sol, et luna stetérunt in habitáculo suo, * in luce sagittárum tuárum, ibunt in splendóre fulgurántis hastæ tuæ.

content.latin: 3:19 In frémitu conculcábis terram: * et in furóre obstupefácies gentes.
content.english: 3:19 In thy anger thou wilt tread the earth under foot: * in thy wrath thou wilt astonish the nations.

segments.t: In frémitu conculcábis terram: * et in furóre obstupefácies gentes.

content.latin: 3:20 Egréssus es in salútem pópuli tui: * in salútem cum Christo tuo.
content.english: 3:20 Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people: * for salvation with thy Christ.

segments.t: Egréssus es in salútem pópuli tui: * in salútem cum Christo tuo.

content.latin: 3:21 Percussísti caput de domo ímpii: * denudásti fundaméntum eius usque ad collum.
content.english: 3:21 Thou struckest the head of the house of the wicked: * thou hast laid bare his foundation even to the neck.

segments.t: Percussísti caput de domo ímpii: * denudásti fundaméntum eius usque ad collum.

content.latin: 3:22 Maledixísti sceptris eius, cápiti bellatórum eius, * veniéntibus ut turbo ad dispergéndum me.
content.english: 3:22 Thou hast cursed his sceptres, the head of his warriors, * them that came out as a whirlwind to scatter me.

segments.t: Maledixísti sceptris eius, cápiti bellatórum eius, * veniéntibus ut turbo ad dispergéndum me.

content.latin: 3:23 Exsultátio eórum * sicut eius, qui dévorat páuperem in abscóndito.
content.english: 3:23 Their joy * was like that of him that devoureth the poor man in secret.

segments.t: Exsultátio eórum * sicut eius, qui dévorat páuperem in abscóndito.

content.latin: 3:24 Viam fecísti in mari equis tuis, * in luto aquárum multárum.
content.english: 3:24 Thou madest a way in the sea for thy horses, * in the mud of many waters.

segments.t: Viam fecísti in mari equis tuis, * in luto aquárum multárum.

content.latin: 3:25 Audívi, et conturbátus est venter meus: * a voce contremuérunt lábia mea.
content.english: 3:25 I have heard and my bowels were troubled: * my lips trembled at the voice.

segments.t: Audívi, et conturbátus est venter meus: * a voce contremuérunt lábia mea.

content.latin: 3:26 Ingrediátur putrédo in óssibus meis, * et subter me scáteat.
content.english: 3:26 Let rottenness enter into my bones, * and swarm under me.

segments.t: Ingrediátur putrédo in óssibus meis, * et subter me scáteat.

content.latin: 3:27 Ut requiéscam in die tribulatiónis: * ut ascéndam ad pópulum accínctum nostrum.
content.english: 3:27 That I may rest in the day of tribulation: * that I may go up to our people that are girded.

segments.t: Ut requiéscam in die tribulatiónis: * ut ascéndam ad pópulum accínctum nostrum.

content.latin: 3:28 Ficus enim non florébit: * et non erit germen in víneis.
content.english: 3:28 For the fig tree shall not blossom: * and there shall be no spring in the vines.

segments.t: Ficus enim non florébit: * et non erit germen in víneis.

content.latin: 3:29 Mentiétur opus olívæ: * et arva non áfferent cibum.
content.english: 3:29 The labour of the olive tree shall fail: * and the fields shall yield no food:

segments.t: Mentiétur opus olívæ: * et arva non áfferent cibum.

content.latin: 3:30 Abscindétur de ovíli pecus: * et non erit arméntum in præsépibus.
content.english: 3:30 The flock shall be cut off from the fold, * and there shall be no herd in the stalls.

segments.t: Abscindétur de ovíli pecus: * et non erit arméntum in præsépibus.

content.latin: 3:31 Ego autem in Dómino gaudébo: * et exsultábo in Deo Iesu meo.
content.english: 3:31 But I will rejoice in the Lord: * and I will joy in God my Jesus.

segments.t: Ego autem in Dómino gaudébo: * et exsultábo in Deo Iesu meo.

content.latin: 3:32 Deus Dóminus fortitúdo mea: * et ponet pedes meos quasi cervórum.
content.english: 3:32 The Lord God is my strength: * and he will make my feet like the feet of harts:

segments.t: Deus Dóminus fortitúdo mea: * et ponet pedes meos quasi cervórum.

content.latin: 3:33 Et super excélsa mea dedúcet me victor * in psalmis canéntem.
content.english: 3:33 And he the conqueror will lead me upon my high places * singing psalms.

segments.t: Et super excélsa mea dedúcet me victor * in psalmis canéntem.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Cum irátus fúeris, Dómine, misericórdiæ recordáberis.
content.english: Ant. When thou art angry, O Lord, thou wilt remember mercy.

segments.t: Ant.
Cum irátus fúeris, Dómine, misericórdiæ recordáberis.

content.latin: Ant. Lauda * Deum tuum, Sion, qui annúntiat iudícia sua Israël.
content.english: Ant. Praise thy God, * O Sion, who declareth his judgments to Israel.

segments.t: Ant.
Lauda * Deum tuum, Sion, qui annúntiat iudícia sua Israël.

content.latin: Psalmus 147 [5]
content.english: Psalm 147 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 147

content.latin: 147:1 Lauda, Ierúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.
content.english: 147:1 Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: * praise thy God, O Sion.

segments.t: Lauda, Ierúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.

content.latin: 147:2 Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.
content.english: 147:2 Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates * he hath blessed thy children within thee.

segments.t: Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.

content.latin: 147:3 Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
content.english: 147:3 Who hath placed peace in thy borders: * and filleth thee with the fat of corn.

segments.t: Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.

content.latin: 147:4 Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo eius.
content.english: 147:4 Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: * his word runneth swiftly.

segments.t: Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo eius.

content.latin: 147:5 Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.
content.english: 147:5 Who giveth snow like wool: * scattereth mists like ashes.

segments.t: Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.

content.latin: 147:6 Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris eius quis sustinébit?
content.english: 147:6 He sendeth his crystal like morsels: * who shall stand before the face of his cold?

segments.t: Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris eius quis sustinébit?

content.latin: 147:7 Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus eius, et fluent aquæ.
content.english: 147:7 He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: * his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.

segments.t: Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus eius, et fluent aquæ.

content.latin: 147:8 Qui annúntiat verbum suum Iacob: * iustítias, et iudícia sua Israël.
content.english: 147:8 Who declareth his word to Jacob: * his justices and his judgments to Israel.

segments.t: Qui annúntiat verbum suum Iacob: * iustítias, et iudícia sua Israël.

content.latin: 147:9 Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et iudícia sua non manifestávit eis.
content.english: 147:9 He hath not done in like manner to every nation: * and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them.

segments.t: Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et iudícia sua non manifestávit eis.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Lauda Deum tuum, Sion, qui annúntiat iudícia sua Israël.
content.english: Ant. Praise thy God, O Sion, who declareth his judgments to Israel.

segments.t: Ant.
Lauda Deum tuum, Sion, qui annúntiat iudícia sua Israël.

content.latin: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
content.english: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

segments.t: Hymnus

content.latin: Ætérna cæli glória,
content.english: O Christ, whose glory fills the heaven,

content.latin: Beáta spes mortálium,
content.english: Our only hope, in mercy given;

content.latin: Summi Tonántis Únice,
content.english: Child of a Virgin meek and pure;

content.latin: Castǽque proles Vírginis:
content.english: Son of the Highest evermore:

content.latin: Da déxteram surgéntibus,
content.english: Grant us thine aid thy praise to sing,

content.latin: Exsúrgat et mens sóbria,
content.english: As opening days new duties bring;

content.latin: Flagrans et in laudem Dei
content.english: That with the light our life may be

content.latin: Grates repéndat débitas.
content.english: Renewed and sanctified by thee.

content.latin: Ortus refúlget Lúcifer,
content.english: The morning star fades from the sky,

content.latin: Præítque solem núntius:
content.english: The sun breaks forth; night’s shadows fly:

content.latin: Cadunt tenébræ nóctium:
content.english: O Thou, true Light, upon us shine:

content.latin: Lux sancta nos illúminet.
content.english: Our darkness turn to light divine.

content.latin: Manénsque nostris sénsibus,
content.english: Within us grant thy light to dwell;

content.latin: Noctem repéllat sǽculi,
content.english: And from our souls dark sins expel;

content.latin: Omníque fine témporis
content.english: Cleanse thou our minds from stain of ill,

content.latin: Purgáta servet péctora.
content.english: And with thy peace our bosoms fill.

content.latin: Quæsíta iam primum fides
content.english: To us strong faith forever give,

content.latin: In corde radíces agat:
content.english: With joyous hope, in thee to live;

content.latin: Secúnda spes congáudeat,
content.english: That life’s rough way may ever be

content.latin: Qua maior exstat cáritas.
content.english: Made strong and pure by charity.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: To God the holy Paraclete,

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Repléti sumus mane misericórdia tua.
content.english: ℣. We are filled in the morning with thy mercy.

segments.t: Repléti sumus mane misericórdia tua.

content.latin: ℟. Exsultávimus, et delectáti sumus.
content.english: ℟. And we have rejoiced, and are delighted.

segments.t: Exsultávimus, et delectáti sumus.

content.latin: Ant. Per víscera misericórdiæ * Dei nostri visitávit nos Óriens ex alto.
content.english: Ant. Through the tender mercy * of our God, the dayspring from on high has visited us.

segments.t: Ant.
Per víscera misericórdiæ * Dei nostri visitávit nos Óriens ex alto.

content.latin: Canticum Zachariæ
content.english: Canticle of Zacharias

segments.t: Canticum Zachariæ

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri visitávit nos Óriens ex alto.

content.latin: Deus, qui virginálem aulam beátæ Maríæ, in qua habitáres, elígere dignátus es: da, quǽsumus; ut, sua nos defensióne munítos, iucúndos fácias suæ interésse festivitáti:
content.english: O God, Who wast pleased to choose for thy dwelling-place the maiden palace of Blessed Mary, grant, we beseech thee, that her protection may shield us, and make us glad in her commemoration.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: Ant. Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
content.english: Ant. Well done, thou good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.

content.latin: ℣. Iustum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas.
content.english: ℣. The Lord guided the just in right paths.

segments.t: Iustum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas.

content.latin: ℟. Et osténdit illi regnum Dei.
content.english: ℟. And showed him the kingdom of God.

segments.t: Et osténdit illi regnum Dei.

content.latin: Deus, qui nos beáti Eusébii Confessóris tui ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut cuius natalítia cólimus, per eius ad te exémpla gradiámur.
content.english: O God, Who, year by year, dost gladden us by the solemn feast-day of thy blessed confessor Eusebius, mercifully grant unto all who keep his birthday, grace to follow his steps toward thee.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
